question: Question linked to image no. 14 A 68-year-old man consults for a loss of general condition in the form of asthenia and anorexia and loss of 12 Kg in the last three months. The physical examination only shows a thin patient and the lesion on the soles of the feet that can be seen in the figure. What do you think is the most likely diagnosis and / or most appropriate attitude?

options.opa: I would look for immune suppression factors, because the lesion seems to correspond to a Norwegian scabies.
options.opb: The skin lesion looks like a callus in a physiological support area, so for now, I would not consider it related to the loss of the general state.
options.opc: The lesion suggests a palmo-plantar form of psoriasis.
options.opd: It seems a form of diffuse seborrheic keratosis associated with age.
options.ope: It suggests a paraneoplastic plantar keratoderma.
